extracted.intended_audience: readers, authors, and publishing professionals interested in Mariner Books and anthology selection
extracted.subtask_description: Describes Mariner Books' editorial mandate and selection preferences for fiction and nonfiction, and explains the Best American Series' anthology selection process and aims. Useful for authors, editors, and anthology contributors seeking to understand what this imprint and series value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mariner Books editorial mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: “Continuing one of the great legacies in American publishing, Mariner Books publishes captivating works of nonfiction and fiction that are thoughtfully engaged with the world we inhabit.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted from Liate Stehlik: the imprint emphasizes captivating work that is thoughtfully engaged with contemporary life; the imprint aims for creativity and energy and to have readers discover their books in the months and years to come.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction should engage the world and interrogate storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: “Fiction is culture! And fiction is craft. ... The fiction we're doing at Mariner engages with the world around us and interrogates the way we tell stories.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kate Nintzel frames fiction as both cultural engagement and craft: novels should interact with present concerns and question/shape narrative form. Examples cited include novels exploring family, gentrification, class satire, and other socially resonant themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish a range including non-precious, fun subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: “We're not precious!” (Mariner publishes both serious work and “fun books” on subjects such as LEGO toys, Bo Jackson, Whitney Houston, and a murder mystery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial program explicitly includes lighter/popular subjects alongside serious literary work — openness to entertaining, accessible, or pop-culture-adjacent books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore the full breadth of subjects and author backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: New Mariner Books titles set out “to explore and interrogate the full breadth of our world,” and are written by “some of today's finest novelists, journalists, historians, sports and travel writers, and scientists.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for wide topical range and disciplinary diversity in authorship (novelists, journalists, historians, scientists, etc.), signaling openness to cross-genre and cross-subject work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backlist curation, reissues, and repackaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Mariner highlights and renews attention to backlist titles (classics and 'hidden gems'), reissuing works and repackaging some authors to create a signature look.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors seek to reprint important but under-read works (examples: Randall Kenan, Ann Petry, Virginia Woolf titles) and to repackage authors (Orwell, Woolf, Philip K. Dick, José Saramago) to bring renewed attention and coherence to the backlist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest-editor model and selection process for Best American Series
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor of each anthology combs through hundreds of journals, magazines, and websites to find the best writing of the year. A guest editor then selects about twenty of those pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series editor (e.g., Heidi Pitlor or Robert Atwan) performs a broad sweep; the guest editor (a leading writer) makes the final curation of ~20 pieces. This two-tiered process is the practical method for assembling the anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthology aim: capture a snapshot of the cultural moment
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our hope is to capture a snapshot of the very cultural moment we are in and a literary time capsule for the people who come after us.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selections are valorized for their cultural resonance and ability to represent the year's literary moment; the series aspires to produce a time capsule rather than merely a 'best-of' by technical merit alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of editorial individuality and diversity in selections
rubrics_metrics.description: “The staying power of the series comes down to the guest editor model. No two people will ever pick the same table of contents. And that keeps it interesting.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness of the guest editor's viewpoint is a feature: diversity of taste and perspective is deliberately embraced so each volume reflects an individual editor's sensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include both established and new authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected pieces are “by both established and new authors.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anthologies and some imprint lists aim to balance recognition of well-known writers with discovery and inclusion of emerging voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic relevance and contemporary resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors praise works that address timely social themes (examples quoted: “exploring what it means to be a family in America today,” “a non-Covidy novel about unexpected isolation,” histories whose themes feel 'ominously familiar today').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for books that illuminate current social, political, or cultural concerns and draw connections between past and present to make work feel resonant and urgent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyrical, inventive use of language and prose worth savoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Praises such as “a lyrical debut,” and “It's always a joy to find a writer whose use of language makes me see the world differently… you want to luxuriate in the playful and inventive portrait.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors value distinctive, lyrical, and inventive prose that rewards slow reading and provides fresh perceptions of the world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical edge and sharp social critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Works described as “a sharp satire of class, wealth, and summer homes.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire that incisively critiques social structures (class, wealth, etc.) is singled out positively in the fiction list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous research combined with imaginative rendering (nonfiction and historical work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions like “rigorously researched, deliciously imagined” and praise for books offering “intimate, insider view” or “character-driven account” of historical periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonfiction and historically rooted books are valued when they combine meticulous research with compelling narrative craft — character-driven storytelling that illuminates contemporary relevance.
